title: Ke olakino a me ke kino
description: Ten short stories about health and the body in Hawaiʻi: a stomach upset, a blood test, training for a canoe voyage, a valley clinic, a football injury, a sickness from a dirty stream, sleep, walking, a lesson at the zoo and stress at work.

lessons.title: Ka ʻōpū o ka lawaiʻa
lessons.summary: Kaʻahanui, a fisherman in Kaunakakai, eats leftover fish that sat out all day, is sick in the night, and the doctor asks him what he ate.
lessons.text:
He lawaiʻa ʻo Kaʻahanui. Noho ʻo ia ma Kaunakakai, ma ka mokupuni ʻo Molokaʻi. I kēlā me kēia lā, hele ʻo ia i ka lawaiʻa i ka hola 5, a hoʻi mai ʻo ia i ka hola 11 me nā iʻa he nui.

I kekahi pō, ua ʻai ʻo Kaʻahanui i ke koena o ka iʻa o nehinei. Ua waiho ʻia ke koena ma luna o ka pākaukau no nā hola he nui. Ma hope o ka ʻai ʻana, ua ʻeha kona ʻōpū. I ka hola 2 o ka pō, ua luaʻi ʻo ia. Ua luaʻi hou ʻo ia i ka hola 3 me ka hapalua.

I ka hola 8 me ka hapalua, ua hele ʻo ia i ka hale lapaʻau. Ua nīnau ke kauka, ʻo Kapuni, iā ia: "Pehea kou ʻōpū?" Ua pane ʻo Kaʻahanui: "ʻEha loa koʻu ʻōpū, a ua luaʻi au i ʻelua manawa." Ua nīnau hou ke kauka: "He aha kāu i ʻai ai i ka pō nei?" Ua pane ʻo ia: "Ua ʻai au i ke koena o ka iʻa." "Ua waiho ʻia ke koena ma hea?" "Ma luna o ka pākaukau, no ʻumi hola."

Ua ʻōlelo ke kauka, ʻaʻole maikaʻi ke koena o ka iʻa i waiho ʻia ma waho no nā hola he nui. "E hoʻomaha ʻoe no hoʻokahi lā," wahi āna. "Mai hele i ka lawaiʻa i kēia lā."

I ka lā aʻe, ua ola hou kona ʻōpū. Ua nīnau kāna wahine iā ia: "Pehea kou ʻōpū i kēia lā?" Ua pane ʻo ia: "Maikaʻi! ʻAʻole au e ʻai hou i ke koena kahiko!" A laila, ua hele hou ka lawaiʻa i ka moana i ka hola 5 me ka hapalua.

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a Kaʻahanui?
He lawaiʻa ʻo ia ma Kaunakakai.
He aha kāna i ʻai ai i kēlā pō?
Ua ʻai ʻo ia i ke koena o ka iʻa o nehinei.
I ka hola ʻehia ʻo ia i luaʻi ai?
Ua luaʻi ʻo ia i ka hola 2, a i ka hola 3 me ka hapalua.
He aha ka nīnau mua a ke kauka?
ʻO "Pehea kou ʻōpū?" ka nīnau mua a ke kauka.
He aha ka pane a Kaʻahanui i ka lā aʻe?
Ua pane ʻo ia, ʻaʻole ʻo ia e ʻai hou i ke koena kahiko.

lessons.title: Ke kui a me ke koko
lessons.summary: Kamakau, seventy, must have a blood test because heart disease runs in her family; she fasts for twelve hours, waits in a slow line with her grandchild, and the needle is not as bad as she feared.
lessons.text:
He 70 makahiki ʻo Kamakau. Noho ʻo ia ma Kāneʻohe me kāna moʻopuna, ʻo Kuʻuipo. He 17 makahiki ʻo Kuʻuipo.

Ua ʻōlelo ke kauka, pono ʻo Kamakau e hana i kekahi hoʻokolohua koko. No ke aha? Aia ka maʻi puʻuwai ma kona moʻokūʻauhau. Ua loaʻa ka maʻi puʻuwai i kona makuahine a me kona kaikuaʻana. "Ma kou moʻokūʻauhau, he nui ka maʻi puʻuwai," wahi a ke kauka. "Pono kākou e nānā i kou koko."

Ma mua o ka hoʻokolohua, ʻaʻole hiki iā Kamakau ke ʻai no ʻumikūmālua hola. Ua ʻai ʻo ia i ka hola 7 o ka pō, a ʻaʻole ʻo ia i ʻai hou a hiki i ka hola 7 o ka lā aʻe. ʻUmikūmālua hola me ka ʻai ʻole!

Ua hopohopo ʻo Kamakau. "Hopohopo au i ke kui," wahi āna. Ua hele pū kāna moʻopuna me ia i ka hale lapaʻau. Ma laila, he laina lōʻihi. Lohi loa ka laina. Ua kū lāua ma ka laina no hoʻokahi hola. "Lohi loa kēia laina!" wahi a Kuʻuipo.

A laila, ua hoʻokomo ke kahu maʻi i ke kui i loko o ka lima o Kamakau. Ua paʻa ʻo Kuʻuipo i ka lima ʻē aʻe o kona kupuna wahine. Ua lawe ke kahu maʻi i kekahi koko mai kona lima. "Ua pau!" wahi a ke kahu maʻi. "ʻAʻole au i ʻike i ke kui!" wahi a Kamakau. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i hopohopo hou.

Ma hope, ua hāʻawi ke kahu maʻi iā ia i kekahi kīʻaha wai. A laila, ua hele lāua i kekahi hale ʻai, a ua kūʻai ʻo Kuʻuipo i ʻelua kīʻaha kope a me ka ʻai no lāua. Ma hope o ʻelua lā, ua kelepona mai ke kauka: maikaʻi ka hopena o ka hoʻokolohua koko.

Nā nīnau:
No ke aha i hana ai ʻo Kamakau i ka hoʻokolohua koko?
No ka mea, aia ka maʻi puʻuwai ma kona moʻokūʻauhau.
Ma mua o ka hoʻokolohua, ʻaʻole hiki iā ia ke ʻai no ʻehia hola?
ʻAʻole hiki iā ia ke ʻai no ʻumikūmālua hola.
Pehea ka laina ma ka hale lapaʻau?
Lōʻihi a lohi loa ka laina.
Ua hopohopo ʻo Kamakau i ke aha?
Ua hopohopo ʻo ia i ke kui.
He aha ka mea a ke kahu maʻi i hāʻawi ai iā ia?
Ua hāʻawi ke kahu maʻi iā ia i kekahi kīʻaha wai.

lessons.title: Ma mua o ka huakaʻi mamao
lessons.summary: Before a long voyage, Kaleikoa's double-canoe crew trains their bodies, swims far out while a guard watches for sharks, practises capsizing a small canoe, and finds and fixes a leak.
lessons.text:
He waʻa kaulua ko ka hui o Kaleikoa ma Honolulu. He ʻelua waʻa ko ka waʻa kaulua, a ua hoʻopaʻa ʻia lāua me nā kaula. I ka makahiki aʻe, e holo ana ka waʻa kaulua i Aotearoa. He huakaʻi mamao loa kēia.

Ma mua o ka huakaʻi, ua hoʻoikaika ka poʻe holo waʻa i ko lākou kino no ʻekolu mahina. Ua holo lākou ma ke kahakai i kēlā me kēia lā, a ua huki lākou i nā kaula kaumaha. Ma kekahi lā, ua ʻau lākou i kahi mamao, i ke kai uliuli ma waho o ke awa. Ua noho kekahi kiaʻi ma kekahi waʻa liʻiliʻi. Ua kiaʻi ʻo ia i ka poʻe ʻau, a ua nānā ʻo ia no nā manō. Ua ʻike ke kiaʻi i kekahi manō, a ua hoʻi koke ka poʻe ʻau i ka waʻa.

Ua aʻo lākou i ka mea e hana ai inā e hoʻokahuli ka nalu i ka waʻa. Ua hoʻokahuli lākou i kekahi waʻa liʻiliʻi ma ke awa, i mea e aʻo ai. Ua hoʻokahuli lākou i ka waʻa i ʻekolu manawa. "Pono kākou e palekana ma ka moana uliuli," wahi a Kaleikoa. "Mamao loa ka ʻāina ma laila."

Ma kekahi lā, ua holo ka waʻa kaulua ma waho o Honolulu. Ua ʻike ʻo Nohealani i ka wai i loko o kekahi o nā waʻa ʻelua. Ua liu ka waʻa! Ua hoʻokahe ka poʻe holo waʻa i ka wai i waho, a ua hoʻi lākou i ke awa. Ma laila, ua hoʻopaʻa ʻo Kaleikoa i kahi i liu ai ka wai. "ʻĀnō, ua palekana ko kākou waʻa kaulua," wahi āna.

Nā nīnau:
Ua hoʻopaʻa ʻia nā waʻa ʻelua o ka waʻa kaulua me ke aha?
Ua hoʻopaʻa ʻia lāua me nā kaula.
Ua kiaʻi ke kiaʻi i wai?
Ua kiaʻi ʻo ia i ka poʻe ʻau, a ua nānā ʻo ia no nā manō.
No ke aha lākou i hoʻokahuli ai i kekahi waʻa liʻiliʻi?
Ua hoʻokahuli lākou i ka waʻa i mea e aʻo ai.
Ua ʻike ʻo Nohealani i ke aha?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka wai i loko o ka waʻa, no ka mea, ua liu ka waʻa.
Ua hana ka poʻe holo waʻa i ke aha me ka wai?
Ua hoʻokahe lākou i ka wai i waho.

lessons.title: Ka hale lapaʻau ma ke awāwa
lessons.summary: A small new clinic opens in Waipiʻo valley, where a healer once worked with plants and seaweed; a devout man blesses it, and Doctor Kalanikau plants a garden of green herbs and fragrant yellow flowers.
lessons.text:
He awāwa lōʻihi ʻo Waipiʻo, ma ka mokupuni ʻo Hawaiʻi. I ka wā kahiko, he kauhale nui ma ke awāwa. Ma ia kauhale, he kahuna lapaʻau. Ua lapaʻau ke kahuna i nā kānaka maʻi me nā lāʻau a me ka limu o ke kai. Ua manaʻoʻiʻo nā kānaka o ke kauhale i ke kahuna lapaʻau.

I kēia makahiki, ua kūkulu ʻia kekahi hale lapaʻau liʻiliʻi hou ma ke awāwa. He kauka ʻo Kalanikau ma laila. Ua hānau ʻia ʻo ia ma Waipiʻo, a ua aʻo ʻo ia ma ke kulanui ma Honolulu.

Ma ka lā mua, ua hoʻolaʻa ʻia ka hale lapaʻau hou. He kanaka haipule ʻo Kahuʻena, a ua pule ʻo ia no ka hale. Ua hoʻolaʻa ʻo ia i ka hale me ka wai o ke kai. Ua hele mai nā kānaka a pau o ke awāwa. He poʻe haipule ka nui o lākou, a ua pule pū lākou.

Ma mua o ka hale, ua kanu ʻo Kalanikau i nā lāʻau ʻōmaʻomaʻo a me nā pua melemele. Nui ke ʻala o nā pua melemele. Ua hele ke ʻala o nā pua ma ke awāwa a pau. Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia: "Ua lapaʻau ke kahuna o ke kauhale kahiko me nā lau ʻōmaʻomaʻo a me ka limu. Manaʻoʻiʻo au he maikaʻi ka ʻike kahiko a me ka ʻike hou."

Nā nīnau:
He aha ma ke awāwa ʻo Waipiʻo i ka wā kahiko?
He kauhale nui ma ke awāwa.
Ua lapaʻau ke kahuna me ke aha?
Ua lapaʻau ʻo ia me nā lāʻau a me ka limu o ke kai.
Ua hoʻolaʻa ʻia ka hale lapaʻau hou e wai?
Ua hoʻolaʻa ʻia e Kahuʻena, he kanaka haipule.
He aha ka mea a Kalanikau i kanu ai?
Ua kanu ʻo ia i nā lāʻau ʻōmaʻomaʻo a me nā pua melemele.
He aha ka manaʻoʻiʻo o Kalanikau?
Manaʻoʻiʻo ʻo ia he maikaʻi ka ʻike kahiko a me ka ʻike hou.

lessons.title: Ka pōpeku ma Kahuku
lessons.summary: Kaʻaukai, number nine on the Kahuku high-school football team, prepares his body, cuts his leg in the dirt in the third game, and the coach cleans and covers it before he plays on.
lessons.text:
He 17 makahiki ʻo Kaʻaukai. Pāʻani ʻo ia i ka pōpeku ma ke kula kiʻekiʻe ma Kahuku, ma Oʻahu. ʻO ʻeiwa kona helu. Kāhea nā kānaka iā ia: "ʻEiwa!"

Hoʻomākaukau ʻo Kaʻaukai i kona kino no ka pōpeku. Holo ʻo ia ma ke kahakai i kēlā me kēia lā. Hoʻoikaika ʻo ia i nā ʻiʻo o kona mau wāwae a me kona mau lima. ʻAi ʻo ia i ka iʻa a me nā hua, no ka mea, hāʻawi ka ʻai maikaʻi i ka ikehu i ke kino. "Me ka ikehu ʻole, ʻaʻohe pōpeku," wahi a kona kumu, ʻo Palakiko.

Ma ke kolu o nā pāʻani o ka makahiki, ua hāʻule ʻo Kaʻaukai ma ka lepo. Ua ʻeha kona wāwae, a ua komo ka lepo i loko o ka ʻeha. Ua holo mai ʻo Palakiko. Ua hoʻokahe ʻo ia i ka wai ma luna o ka wāwae, a maʻemaʻe ka ʻeha. "Pono e maʻemaʻe ka ʻeha," wahi āna. A laila, ua uhi ʻo ia i ka ʻeha me kekahi uhi keʻokeʻo.

Ua hoʻi ʻo Kaʻaukai i ke kahua. Ua holo ʻo ia me ka ikehu nui a hiki i ka pau ʻana o ka pāʻani, a ua lanakila ko Kahuku kime. Ma hope, ua ʻōlelo ʻo Palakiko, ʻo ʻEiwa ka mea pāʻani poʻokela o ka pāʻani. Ua ʻakaʻaka ʻo Kaʻaukai. "ʻAʻole au he poʻokela," wahi āna. "Poʻokela ko kākou kime!"

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka helu o Kaʻaukai?
ʻO ʻeiwa kona helu.
Pehea ʻo Kaʻaukai e hoʻomākaukau ai i kona kino?
Holo ʻo ia ma ke kahakai, a hoʻoikaika ʻo ia i kona mau ʻiʻo.
He aha ka hopena ma ke kolu o nā pāʻani?
Ua hāʻule ʻo ia ma ka lepo, a ua ʻeha kona wāwae.
Ua hana ʻo Palakiko i ke aha?
Ua hoʻokahe ʻo ia i ka wai ma luna o ka ʻeha a maʻemaʻe, a ua uhi ʻo ia i ka ʻeha.
ʻO wai ka mea pāʻani poʻokela?
ʻO Kaʻaukai ka mea pāʻani poʻokela.

lessons.title: Ka ʻōpala ma ke kahawai
lessons.summary: When a sickness spreads among children in Wailuku, the news traces it to rubbish in the stream; the mayor cleans it up, and a senator brings a new rubbish policy to the legislature with federal money.
lessons.text:
I kekahi mahina, ua laha kekahi maʻi ma waena o nā keiki o Wailuku, ma Maui. Ua ʻeha ko lākou ʻōpū, a ua luaʻi kekahi o lākou. Ua laha ka maʻi mai kekahi kula a i kekahi kula ʻē aʻe.

Ua noiʻi nā kauka. Ua ʻike lākou he nui ka ʻōpala i loko o ke kahawai ma kahi kokoke i nā kula. Ua pāʻani nā keiki ma ka wai o ke kahawai, me ka ʻōpala. Ua hōʻike ʻia ka nūhou ma ka nūpepa a ma ka lekiō. Ua kākau ka nūpepa: "Ua laha ka maʻi ma muli o ka ʻōpala." Ua kamaʻilio ka pāpaho a pau no kēia nūhou.

Ua hele ka meia o Maui, ʻo Kamaʻehu, i ke kahawai. Ua hui pū ʻo ia me nā kānaka o ke kaiāulu, a ua lawe lākou i ka ʻōpala a pau mai ke kahawai aku. Ua ʻōlelo ka meia i ka pāpaho, ua maʻemaʻe ke kahawai ʻānō.

Akā ua manaʻo ke kenekoa ʻo Kahoʻonei, pono kekahi kulekele hou. Ua hele ʻo ia i ka ʻahaʻōlelo ma Honolulu. Ma ka ʻahaʻōlelo, ua hōʻike ke kenekoa i kona kulekele: ʻaʻole e waiho ʻia ka ʻōpala ma kahi kokoke i ke kahawai. Ua ʻae ka ʻahaʻōlelo i ke kulekele. Ua hāʻawi pū ke aupuni pekelala i kekahi kālā, i mea e mālama ai i nā kahawai. Ua kākau ka nūpepa i kēia nūhou: he kālā pekelala no nā kahawai o Maui.

Nā nīnau:
Ua laha ka maʻi ma waena o wai?
Ua laha ka maʻi ma waena o nā keiki o Wailuku.
He aha ka mea i loko o ke kahawai?
He nui ka ʻōpala i loko o ke kahawai.
ʻO wai ka meia o Maui?
ʻO Kamaʻehu ka meia o Maui.
Ua hele ke kenekoa i hea?
Ua hele ʻo ia i ka ʻahaʻōlelo ma Honolulu.
Ua hāʻawi ke aupuni pekelala i ke aha?
Ua hāʻawi ke aupuni pekelala i kekahi kālā no nā kahawai.

lessons.title: Ka polopeka i hiki ʻole ke moe
lessons.summary: Professor Kaʻaumoana, who teaches mathematics in Mānoa, has a full calendar and cannot sleep; the doctor tells him to keep free time, so he drinks tea, listens to guitar music and sleeps beside his cat.
lessons.text:
He polopeka ʻo Kaʻaumoana ma ke kulanui ma Mānoa. Aʻo ʻo ia i ka makemakika. Aloha ʻo ia i ka makemakika, akā nui loa kāna hana. Piha kona ʻalemanaka. Ma kona ʻalemanaka, he pūkaʻina haʻawina makemakika i kēlā me kēia lā, a he mau hālāwai i ka pō. ʻAʻohe manawa kaʻawale.

I kēlā me kēia pō, ʻaʻole hiki i ka polopeka ke moe. Noʻonoʻo ʻo ia i ka makemakika. Ua moe ʻo ia no ʻekolu hola wale nō i ka pō. Ma ka haʻawina, ua ʻike kāna mau haumāna, ʻaʻole ʻo ia i moe.

Ua hele ʻo ia i ke kauka. Ua ʻōlelo ke kauka, pono ʻo ia e hoʻomaha. "E kākau i kekahi manawa kaʻawale ma kou ʻalemanaka," wahi a ke kauka, "e like me kekahi haʻawina. Ma mua o ka moe ʻana, mai hana i ka makemakika. E hoʻomākaukau i kekahi kīʻaha kī, a e hoʻolohe i ke mele."

I kēlā pō, ua hoʻomākaukau ka polopeka i kekahi kīʻaha kī wela. Ua hoʻolohe ʻo ia i kekahi mele kahiko me ke kīkā. Ua hoʻolohe ʻo ia i ka puana o ke mele, a ua hīmeni pū ʻo ia i ka puana. Ma hope, ua hoʻokani ʻo ia i kāna kīkā kahiko. Ua lele mai kāna pōpoki, ʻo Popo, ma luna o kona wahi moe. Ua moe ka pōpoki, a ua moe pū ka polopeka a hiki i ka hola 7.

Nā nīnau:
Aʻo ka polopeka i ke aha?
Aʻo ʻo ia i ka makemakika.
He aha ka mea ma kona ʻalemanaka?
He pūkaʻina haʻawina a me nā hālāwai.
Ua ʻōlelo ke kauka he aha?
Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia, pono ka polopeka e kākau i kekahi manawa kaʻawale ma kona ʻalemanaka.
Ua hoʻolohe ʻo ia i ke aha?
Ua hoʻolohe ʻo ia i kekahi mele kahiko me ke kīkā.
ʻO wai ka inoa o ka pōpoki?
ʻO Popo ka inoa o ka pōpoki.

lessons.title: He ʻumi kaukani kapuaʻi
lessons.summary: Hiapo's new watch counts his steps, so he climbs a mountain trail on Kauaʻi past round stones, hills and riders on horses, runs out of water, and a visitor shares hers.
lessons.text:
He 45 makahiki ʻo Hiapo. Noho ʻo ia ma Līhuʻe, ma Kauaʻi. Ua ʻōlelo kona kauka, pono ʻo ia e hele wāwae i kēlā me kēia lā. Ua hāʻawi kāna kaikamahine iā ia i kekahi hāmeʻa hou no kona lima. Helu ka hāmeʻa i kona mau kapuaʻi. "E hele wāwae i ʻumi kaukani kapuaʻi i ka lā," wahi a kāna kaikamahine.

I kekahi Pōʻaono, ua hele ʻo Hiapo i kekahi kuahiwi ma kahi kokoke i Līhuʻe. Laulā ke alahele ma lalo o ke kuahiwi. Ma ke alahele laulā, he nui nā pōhaku poepoe. Ua hele wāwae ʻo ia ma luna o kekahi puʻu, a laila ma luna o kekahi puʻu ʻē aʻe. ʻAʻole laulā ke alahele ma luna, ma kahi kokoke i ka piko o ke kuahiwi.

Ma ke alahele, ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi hui mākaʻikaʻi ma luna o nā lio. Ua holo nā lio ma ke alahele laulā. Ua aloha aku ʻo Hiapo i ka poʻe mākaʻikaʻi.

I ka hola 11, ua nele ʻo Hiapo i ka wai. Ua pau kāna wai a pau. Ua ʻike kekahi wahine mākaʻikaʻi ua nele ʻo Hiapo i ka wai. Ua pau ka wai o ka hui a pau, koe ka wai o kēia wahine. Ua hāʻawi ʻo ia i kekahi o kāna wai iā Hiapo. "Mahalo!" wahi a Hiapo.

Ma ka pau ʻana o ka lā, ua nānā ʻo Hiapo i kāna hāmeʻa. He ʻumikūmālua kaukani kapuaʻi! Ua ʻoi aku ka nui ma mua o ka ʻumi kaukani. "E hoʻi hou ana au i ke kuahiwi," wahi āna, "akā me ka wai nui!"

Nā nīnau:
He aha ka hana a ka hāmeʻa hou?
Helu ka hāmeʻa i nā kapuaʻi o Hiapo.
Pehea ke alahele ma lalo o ke kuahiwi?
Laulā ke alahele, a he nui nā pōhaku poepoe.
Ua ʻike ʻo Hiapo i ke aha ma luna o nā lio?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i kekahi hui mākaʻikaʻi.
Ua nele ʻo Hiapo i ke aha?
Ua nele ʻo ia i ka wai.
Ua pau ka wai o ka hui mākaʻikaʻi a pau?
ʻAʻole, ua pau ka wai o ka hui a pau, koe kekahi wahine.
ʻEhia kapuaʻi ma ka hāmeʻa i ka pau ʻana o ka lā?
He ʻumikūmālua kaukani kapuaʻi.

lessons.title: Ka liona a me ke kanaka
lessons.summary: Kamalani's class visits the lions at the Honolulu zoo; behind the glass the lion hides and then shows its frightening teeth, and the children write on paper how a lion's body is like a person's.
lessons.text:
Ua hele ʻo Kamalani a me kāna papa i ke kahua holoholona ma Honolulu. He 10 makahiki ʻo Kamalani. ʻO Kahale ka inoa o kāna kumu. Ke aʻo nei ka papa no ke kino.

Ua hele ka papa i kahi o nā liona. Ua kū nā keiki ma hope o kekahi aniani nui. Ma kēlā ʻaoʻao o ke aniani, ua huna kekahi liona ma hope o kekahi lāʻau. ʻAʻole i ʻike nā keiki i ka liona. "Aia ka liona i hea?" wahi a Kamalani. "Ke huna nei ʻo ia," wahi a Kahale.

Ma hope, ua hele mai ka liona i ke aniani. Ua wehe ʻo ia i kona waha nui. Weliweli kona mau niho! Ua hoʻi nā keiki i hope. "Weliweli!" wahi a Kamalani. "Mai hopohopo," wahi a Kahale. "Palekana kākou ma hope o ke aniani."

Ua hāʻawi ke kumu i ka pepa i kēlā me kēia keiki. "He māmela ka liona," wahi āna, "a he māmela pū ke kanaka. He aha nā mea kūlike o ke kino o ka liona a me ke kino o ke kanaka?" Ua kākau nā keiki ma ka pepa: he koko ʻulaʻula ko lāua, he puʻuwai ko lāua, he mau maka ko lāua. Ua kūlike ke kino o ka liona me ke kino o ke kanaka ma nā mea he nui.

Ua nīnau ʻo Kamalani: "He ʻenemi ko ka liona?" Ua pane ʻo Kahale: "ʻAʻohe ʻenemi nui o ka liona, koe ke kanaka."

Nā nīnau:
Ua hele ka papa i hea?
Ua hele ka papa i ke kahua holoholona ma Honolulu.
Ua huna ka liona ma hea?
Ua huna ka liona ma hope o kekahi lāʻau.
Pehea nā niho o ka liona?
Weliweli nā niho o ka liona.
He māmela ka liona?
ʻAe, he māmela ka liona, a he māmela pū ke kanaka.
He aha ka mea a nā keiki i kākau ai ma ka pepa?
Ua kākau lākou i nā mea kūlike o ke kino o ka liona a me ke kino o ke kanaka.

lessons.title: Ka pāʻina a Kaʻiulani
lessons.summary: Kaʻiulani works day and night in her small business, stops seeing her friends and lies that she is fine; at a party her friend sees the problem, Kaʻiulani apologises and changes her way of life.
lessons.text:
He pāʻoihana liʻiliʻi kā Kaʻiulani ma Kahului, ma Maui. Kūʻai aku ʻo ia i nā lei a me nā ʻaʻahu. Hana ʻo ia ma kāna pāʻoihana i ke ao a me ka pō. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i launa me kona mau hoaaloha no nā mahina he nui. Ma mua, ua launa pū lākou i kēlā me kēia pule.

Ua kelepona mai kona hoaaloha, ʻo Kaʻikena, i kēlā me kēia pule. "Pehea ʻoe?" wahi āna. "Maikaʻi au," wahi a Kaʻiulani. Akā ua hoʻopunipuni ʻo ia. ʻAʻole ʻo ia i maikaʻi. Ua ʻeha kona poʻo, a ʻaʻole ʻo ia i moe maikaʻi. Ua hoʻopunipuni ʻo ia i kona hoaaloha, a ua hoʻopunipuni pū ʻo ia iā ia iho.

I kekahi Pōʻaono, he pāʻina ma ka hale o Kaʻikena. Ua hele ʻo Kaʻiulani i ka pāʻina. Ma ka pāʻina, ua nānā ʻo Kaʻikena iā ia e like me kekahi kiu ma kekahi kiʻiʻoniʻoni kiu. Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka hihia. "He hihia kou," wahi a Kaʻikena. "Nui loa kāu hana."

Ua ʻae ʻo Kaʻiulani. "E kala mai iaʻu," wahi āna. "Ua hoʻopunipuni au iā ʻoe." "Ua kala au iā ʻoe," wahi a Kaʻikena. "Akā pono ʻoe e hoʻohuli i kou nohona."

Ua hoʻohuli ʻo Kaʻiulani i kona nohona. ʻĀnō, pani ʻo ia i kāna pāʻoihana i ka hola 5. Launa ʻo ia me kona mau hoaaloha i kēlā me kēia Pōʻaono, a heluhelu ʻo ia i nā puke kiu ma ka pō. Moe maikaʻi ʻo ia, a ʻaʻole ʻeha kona poʻo.

Nā nīnau:
He aha kā Kaʻiulani pāʻoihana?
Kūʻai aku ʻo ia i nā lei a me nā ʻaʻahu ma Kahului.
Ua hoʻopunipuni ʻo Kaʻiulani i kona hoaaloha pehea?
Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia, maikaʻi ʻo ia, akā ʻaʻole ʻo ia i maikaʻi.
Ua ʻike ʻo Kaʻikena i ka hihia ma hea?
Ua ʻike ʻo ia i ka hihia ma ka pāʻina.
Ua ʻōlelo ʻo Kaʻiulani he aha?
Ua ʻōlelo ʻo ia: "E kala mai iaʻu."
Ua hoʻohuli ʻo Kaʻiulani i kona nohona pehea?
Pani ʻo ia i kāna pāʻoihana i ka hola 5, a launa ʻo ia me kona mau hoaaloha.
